text: He poured dry sand underneath a five-hundred-ton stone bridge.
You see, two teams are racing to build the longest stone arch bridge across a roaring river.
When the chief architect sees a junior engineer filling iron cylinders with beach sand under the main support beams,
his face turns red:
"Are you out of your mind? One rainstorm and this whole bridge washes into the river!"
But the kid doesn't say a word.
He just seals the boxes tight.
Months later, both bridges are finished.
Now comes the hardest part:
removing the wooden supports without the heavy stones collapsing.
The rival team grabs axes and saws to chop their timber out.
With every swing, the massive stones shift violently,
until a jagged crack shoots straight through their arch.
On the other bridge, the chief architect is sweating bullets, waiting for disaster.
Meanwhile, the young engineer calmly walks underneath the massive arch with a tiny wrench.
He kneels down next to the iron boxes...
and unscrews a small plug at the bottom.
Instantly, dry sand begins pouring out like a giant hourglass.
Millimeter by millimeter, the wooden supports lower smoothly,
allowing the five-hundred-ton stone bridge to lock into place without a single crack.
